A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying work on diversity bonuses for imitation learning with PPGA, despite substantial retitling and revision. All 22 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original locomotion experiments, component ablations, demonstration-count studies, and imitation-from-observation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original locomotion comparisons, bonus-weight and demonstration studies, varied behavioral measures, and adaptation experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v1's measure-conditioned GAIL/VAIL models and p + qI bonus are replaced by unconditioned EBC variants with a qI bonus; v2 also introduces DiffAIL-EBC. Archive selection changes in the specified procedure from learned-reward fitness in v1 Algorithm 1 to oracle fitness in v2 Section 3 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: The three original locomotion environments remain, while v2 adds Hopper, Ant, tasks using jump height and yaw measures, true-reward QD-RL, and hurdles, motor-failure, and friction perturbations. The observation-only imitation setting reported in v1 Table 2 and Appendix I is removed.

E2.justification: The main comparison adds DiffAIL and removes PWIL between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 8. GAIL, VAIL, AIRL, GIRIL, Max-Ent IRL, and PPGA with true reward remain, making this a limited revision of comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported protocol changes archive selection to oracle fitness and bonus settings from p = q = 0.5 to q = 2. v2 adds CCDF evaluation and exhaustive archive-skill selection without retraining for adaptation. Demonstration-count experiments change from Walker2d with 1, 2, and 4 demonstrations to Humanoid with 1, 2, 4, and 10, plus diversity controls.

E4.justification: The separate measure-bonus and measure-conditioning ablations in v1 Section 5.4 and Appendix E disappear. v2 adds bonus-weight sensitivity, behavioral-measure generality tests, and three perturbation robustness studies, while substantially revising the demonstration study to examine quantity, diversity, and quality.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averages and standard-deviation bands. v2 additionally reports standard deviations throughout the main numerical comparison, introduces Tukey HSD tests, and uses interquartile means with 95% confidence intervals for adaptation based on two archives.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 8, reported Humanoid PPGA QD-Score changes from 5.71 million to 7.38 million; MConbo-GAIL's 8.47 million is replaced by GAIL-EBC's 5.31 million. Numerous DiffAIL, measure, adaptation, and sensitivity results are added, while PWIL and observation-only results disappear. Method and archive-fitness changes preclude treating these replacements as same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The central indicator-reward lemma and Bayes-rule proof are retained from v1 Appendix G in v2 Section 3.1. Mathematical changes include added DiffAIL noise-prediction formulations and removed PWIL and observation-only formulations. v2 also introduces an inconsistent GAIL loss in Equation 7 relative to Algorithm 3.

C1.justification: v2 drops measure conditioning and QD-IFO as contributions and centers the paper on EBC, including an explicit contribution to QD-RL. The abstract replaces the 2×-expert headline with approximately 20% above expert performance in Humanoid and adds claims concerning DiffAIL.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes generalization through measure conditioning; v2 focuses on behavioral curiosity and discusses why reward shaping can improve true-reward PPGA. Its expanded limitations report performance declines when archives use learned fitness and restrict direct applicability to MDPs and policy-gradient optimization. New discussion addresses demonstration diversity and episode-level credit assignment.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link, discloses approximately two days on one A40 GPU per experiment, and supplies DiffAIL's variance schedule and adaptation implementation details. Most existing PPGA/AIL hyperparameters, demonstration statistics, and hardware specifications are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the contribution against intrinsic curiosity, Yu et al. (2025)'s single-step behavioral bonuses, multi-domain imitation, and hierarchical skill discovery. It adds DiffAIL, adaptation, and human-feedback QD references while removing earlier PWIL, IDIL, IQ-learn, and observation-only coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around EBC and QD-IRL. Background and related work are reorganized, the proof and main algorithm move into the main text, and the appendices are substantially restructured with additional discussion sections.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, removes the introductory illustrations, revises the workflow diagram, and consolidates the separate GAIL/VAIL learning-curve figures into a combined comparison including DiffAIL. The main results table moves to the appendix with uncertainty entries, and new adaptation, sensitivity, CCDF, and statistical displays are added.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation of the exploration bonus through varied measures, controlled demonstration studies, perturbation tests, and additional statistical reporting. However, oracle-fitness archive selection narrows v1's reward-unavailable formulation, and the new 'few-shot' evaluation exhaustively searches archives. Table 9 also labels the Halfcheetah VAIL effect negative despite the higher VAIL-EBC mean in Table 8. These gains and substantive qualifications leave the net overall quality change uncertain.
